subject.title: [Feature]: feat(session-memory): Add auto-trigger on idle, shutdown, and periodic checkpoints

question: Which lifecycle and privacy contract should OpenClaw support for automatic session-memory checkpoints beyond explicit /new and /reset commands?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the permanent shape affects internal hook events, plugin-visible lifecycle behavior, shutdown deadlines, new config keys, and private transcript retention/provider processing.

options.title: Stage the lifecycle contract
options.body: First accept or replace the daily/idle reset path, then design shutdown, periodic checkpoint, and summary-output behavior as explicit opt-in surfaces with dedupe and privacy rules.

options.title: Narrow to reset persistence
options.body: Keep the immediate work limited to automatic daily/idle reset memory persistence and split shutdown, message-count checkpoints, and LLM summary output into separate follow-ups.

options.title: Move optional checkpointing to plugins
options.body: Define any missing generic lifecycle API and let a memory plugin or ClawHub package own optional checkpointing instead of expanding the bundled hook.

recommendation.title: Stage the lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: First accept or replace the daily/idle reset path, then design shutdown, periodic checkpoint, and summary-output behavior as explicit opt-in surfaces with dedupe and privacy rules.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest combined signal from the current hook architecture history and the prior detailed review on this exact issue.
